verses.text: Joab was told, "The king is crying and mourning for Absalom."
So for the whole army, the victory that day turned into mourning, because the soldiers heard people say, "The king is grieving for his son."
That day the soldiers crept quietly into the city, like soldiers who are ashamed because they ran away from battle.
The king covered his face and cried loudly, "My son Absalom! Absalom, my son, my son!"
Then Joab went into the house to the king and said, "Today you have shamed all your men. They saved your life today, and the lives of your sons and daughters, your wives and your slave wives.

You love those who hate you, and you hate those who love you. Today you have made it clear that your commanders and soldiers mean nothing to you. I can see that you would be happy if Absalom were alive today and all of us were dead.

Now get up, go out, and encourage your men. I promise by the LORD that if you don't go out, not one man will be left with you by tonight. That would be worse for you than all the trouble you have had from your youth until now."
So the king got up and sat at the city gate. When the people were told, "The king is sitting at the gate," they all came to him. Meanwhile, the Israelites had all run away to their homes.

All through the tribes of Israel, the people were arguing with each other. They said, "The king rescued us from our enemies. He saved us from the Philistines. But now he has run away from the land because of Absalom.
And Absalom, whom we anointed to rule over us, has died in battle. So why is no one talking about bringing the king back?"

King David sent a message to the priests Zadok and Abiathar: "Ask the leaders of Judah, 'Why are you the last to bring the king back to his palace? I have heard what all Israel is saying about bringing the king back to his home.
You are my relatives, my own flesh and blood. So why should you be the last to bring the king back?'
And tell Amasa, 'You are my own flesh and blood. May God punish me, and even more, if I do not make you commander of my army from now on in place of Joab.'"
So David won the hearts of all the men of Judah, and they were united as one. They sent word to the king: "Come back, you and all your officials."
So the king started back and came to the Jordan River. The men of Judah came to Gilgal to meet the king and bring him across the Jordan.
Shimei son of Gera, from the tribe of Benjamin, who lived in Bahurim, hurried down with the men of Judah to meet King David.
A thousand men from Benjamin were with him. Ziba, the servant of Saul's family, was there too, with his fifteen sons and twenty servants. They rushed into the Jordan to meet the king.
They crossed back and forth to bring the king's family over and to do whatever the king wanted. As the king was about to cross the Jordan, Shimei son of Gera fell down in front of him.
He said to the king, "My lord, please don't hold me guilty. Don't remember the wrong your servant did on the day you left Jerusalem. Please put it out of your mind.
I, your servant, know that I have sinned. That is why I have come today, the first from all the tribes of Joseph to come down and meet my lord the king."
But Abishai son of Zeruiah said, "Shouldn't Shimei be put to death for this? He cursed the LORD's chosen king!"

David said, "What has this got to do with you, sons of Zeruiah? Why are you acting like my enemies today? Should anyone in Israel be put to death today? Don't I know that today I am king over Israel again?"
So the king said to Shimei, "You will not die." And the king made him a promise with an oath.
Mephibosheth, Saul's grandson, also came down to meet the king. He had not cared for his feet, trimmed his beard, or washed his clothes from the day the king left until the day he came back safely.
When he came from Jerusalem to meet the king, the king asked him, "Mephibosheth, why didn't you go with me?"
He answered, "My lord the king, my servant tricked me. I said, 'Saddle a donkey for me so I can ride with the king,' because I, your servant, am crippled.
But Ziba has told lies about me to you, my lord the king. But my lord the king is like an angel of God, so do whatever you think is right.

All my grandfather's family deserved nothing but death from my lord the king. Yet you gave me a place among those who eat at your own table. So what right do I have to ask anything more from the king?"
The king said to him, "Why say any more? I have decided that you and Ziba will divide the land between you."
Mephibosheth said to the king, "Let him take it all! It is enough for me that my lord the king has come home safely."
Barzillai from Gilead also came down from Rogelim. He went with the king to the Jordan to see him safely across.
Barzillai was very old, eighty years old. He had provided food for the king while he stayed at Mahanaim, because he was a very rich man.
The king said to Barzillai, "Come with me to Jerusalem, and I will take care of you there."
But Barzillai answered the king, "How many more years do I have to live, that I should go up to Jerusalem with the king?

Today I am eighty years old. Can I still tell what is good and what is bad? Can your servant taste what he eats and drinks? Can I still hear the voices of men and women singing? Why should your servant be an extra burden to my lord the king?
Your servant will just go a little way across the Jordan with the king. Why should the king give me such a reward?

Please let your servant go back, so I can die in my own town near the grave of my father and mother. But here is your servant Kimham. Let him go with my lord the king, and do for him whatever you think is good."
The king answered, "Kimham will go with me, and I will do for him whatever you think is good. And whatever you ask of me, I will do for you."
So all the people crossed the Jordan, and then the king crossed. The king kissed Barzillai and blessed him, and Barzillai went back home.
The king went on to Gilgal, and Kimham went with him. All the soldiers of Judah and half the soldiers of Israel went with the king.

Soon all the men of Israel came to the king and said to him, "Why did our brothers, the men of Judah, steal the king away? Why did they bring the king and his family across the Jordan, together with all David's men?"
All the men of Judah answered the men of Israel, "Because the king is our close relative. Why are you angry about this? Have we eaten any of the king's food? Has he given us any gifts?"

The men of Israel answered the men of Judah, "We have ten shares in the king, so we have more right to David than you do. Why did you treat us with contempt? Weren't we the first to speak about bringing back our king?" But the men of Judah spoke even more harshly than the men of Israel.
